nodes.name: Theorem C.1: Sample Efficient Algorithm Agnostic
nodes.statement:
Suppose 2, 1 hold, allow ${H^\star}\not\in \mathdutchcal{H}$, and define $\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}\coloneqq \inf_{H\in \mathdutchcal{H}} \euscr{D}^\star(H\triangle {H^\star})$.
        Fix any parameters $\varepsilon,\delta, \gamma \in (0,\nicefrac{1}{2})$ with $\varepsilon\geq \gamma > {\nicefrac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}{\alpha}}$.  
        Consider the Pessimistic-ERM{} instance defined with respect to $n=\widetilde{O}\left(\left(\nicefrac{1}{\varepsilon}\right)\cdot \left(\textrm{\rm VC}{}(\mathdutchcal{H})+\log{\nicefrac{1}{\delta}}\right)\right)$  positive and unlabeled samples obtained from the two streams in the PIU learning model (1).
        Then, with probability $1-\delta$, any hypothesis $H\in \mathdutchcal{H}$ that satisfies:
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item $H$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with tolerance $\rho= \gamma $; and 
            \item $H$ is optimal (though not necessarily feasible) for Pessimistic-ERM{} with tolerance $\rho= {5\varepsilon} $,
        \end{enumerate}
        also satisfies
        \[
            \euscr{D}^\star\left(H\triangle {H^\star}\right) \leq 
                \frac{144}{\sigma^2}\cdot \, \varepsilon^{1/q^2}
                \,.
        \]

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1: Sample Efficient Algorithm Realizable
nodes.statement:
Suppose 1 holds. 
    Fix any $\varepsilon,\delta\in (0,\nicefrac{1}{2})$.
    There is an algorithm that, given $\varepsilon,\delta$ and $n=\widetilde{O}\big({{(\varepsilon \sigma)}}^{-2q}\cdot \left(\textrm{\rm VC}{}(\mathdutchcal{H})+\log{\nicefrac{1}{\delta}}\right)\big)$ independent samples from $\euscr{P}^\star$ and $\euscr{D}$, outputs a hypothesis $\widehat{h}$ such that, with probability $1-\delta$,
    \[ 
        \Pr_{\euscr{D}^\star}\big(\widehat{h}(x)\neq h^\star(x)\big)\leq \varepsilon\,.
    \]

nodes.name: Lemma C.2: Upper bound on False Negative Error…
nodes.statement:
Fix any $\eta\in (0,1).$
            Under the setting of C.1, consider any hypothesis $T\in \mathdutchcal{H}$ feasible for the Pessimistic-ERM{} instance in C.1 with tolerance $\rho=\eta$.
            Then, with probability $1-\left(\nicefrac{\delta}{2}\right)$,
            \[
                \euscr{D}^\star\left({H^\star}\setminus T\right) \leq \eta+\sqrt{\eta\varepsilon}+\varepsilon\,.
            \]
            In particular, for $T=H$ and $\gamma\leq \varepsilon$, with probability $1-\left(\nicefrac{\delta}{2}\right)$, $\euscr{D}^\star\left({H^\star} \setminus H\right)\leq 3\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Lemma C.7: $\euscr{D}(H)-\euscr{D}(H')~{\leq}~\mathrm{poly}_q(\varepsilon)$
nodes.statement:
Let $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$ be the event that the uniform convergence bounds in 4.1 hold for both the positive samples $P$ and the unlabeled samples $U$, and the hypothesis classes $\mathdutchcal{H}\cup\left\{G^c\colon G\in \mathdutchcal{H}\right\}\cup \left\{G\setminus ({H^\star} \cap H\cap H')\colon G\in \mathdutchcal{H}\right\}$.
                Then, $\Pr[\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}]\geq 1-(\nicefrac{\delta}{4})$.
                Moreover, conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$, 
                \[
                    \euscr{D}(H) - \euscr{D}(H')
                    \leq \frac{11}{\sigma} \, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                    \,.
                \]

nodes.name: Lemma C.5: Feasibility of $H'$
nodes.statement:
Let $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$ be the event that the uniform convergence bounds in 4.1 hold for the positive samples $P$ and the hypothesis class $\mathdutchcal{H}\cup\left\{G^c\colon G\in \mathdutchcal{H}\right\}$.
                Then, $\Pr[\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}]\geq 1-(\nicefrac{\delta}{4})$.
                Moreover, conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$, $H'$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} defined by samples $(P,U)$ with $\rho=5\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.1: Second-Order Uniform Convergence from Boucheron_Bousquet_Lugosi_2005
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathdutchcal{F}$ be any concept class on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finite VC-dimension, \textit{i.e.}{}, $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\mathdutchcal{F})}<\infty$, and let $\euscr{D}$ be any distribution over $\mathbb{R}^d$.
        For any confidence level $\delta\in (0,\nicefrac{1}{2})$ and any fixed set $F^\star\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, with probability $1-\delta$, over the draw $X\sim \euscr{D}^n$, every $F\in \mathdutchcal{F}$,
        \begin{align*}
            \euscr{D}(F\triangle F^\star)
                &\leq 
                    D_n(F\triangle F^\star)
                    + \sqrt{
                        D_n(F\triangle F^\star)
                        \cdot 
                        s(\mathdutchcal{F},n,\delta)
                    }
                    + 
                    4 s(\mathdutchcal{F},n,\delta)\,,
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\\
                D_n(F\triangle F^\star)
                &\leq 
                    \euscr{D}(F\triangle F^\star)
                    + \sqrt{
                        \euscr{D}(F\triangle F^\star)
                        \cdot 
                        s(\mathdutchcal{F},n,\delta)
                    }
                    + 
                    4 s(\mathdutchcal{F},n,\delta)\,,
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}
        \end{align*}
        where $s(\mathdutchcal{F},n,\delta)$ and $D_n(F\triangle F^\star)$ are defined as follows 
        \[
            s(\mathdutchcal{F},n,\delta) \coloneqq \frac{2\textrm{\rm VC}{(\mathdutchcal{F})}\log{(n+1)}+\log{\nicefrac{4}{\delta}}}{n}
            \qquad\text{and}\qquad
            D_n(F\triangle F^\star)
            \coloneqq 
            \frac{\left| X\cap (F\triangle F^\star) \right|}{\left| X \right|}\,.
        \]
